newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Nera sees US$1 bln global revenue by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Nera sees US$1 bln global revenue by 2000.

text.p: Norwegian telecommunications company Nera ASA said on Friday it expected its global revenue to reach about US$1 billion by the year 2000 with about half the revenue coming from Asia.

Nera's executive chairman Frode Botnevik told Reuters the group had a worldwide turnover of 2.63 billion crowns (US$395 million) in 1996, of which slightly under 40 percent came from the Asian region.
"For the group as a whole, we forecast that from 1996 to 2000, (revenue) will grow by approximately two and half times to basically US$1 billion," Botnevik said in an interview.

"With the rapid growth in the Asian economies, hopefully within a couple of years already more than 50 percent of the revenue will come from this region and as we go forward perhaps even more," he added.
Nera has received in-principle approval for listing of its shares on the main board of the Stock Exchange of Singapore.
The company, which makes transmission systems for the telecomunications market, already has a primary listing on the Oslo bourse and a secondary listing on NASDAQ in New York.

Botnevik said the company's growth in Asia was being driven mainly by the rapid liberalisation of the telecommunications markets which was forcing existing players and new competitors to install new networks with high quality, high speed equipment.
